title: The inverse image of the direct image of a constant sheaf of sets on a closed subset is the direct image of the constant sheaf on the preimage
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces, $W\subseteq Y$ a closed subset, $Z=f^{-1}(W)$ (closed in $X$) and $R$ a set. For a closed subset $C$ of a topological space $T$ with inclusion $i_C$ let $(i_C)_*\underline R_C$ be the sheaf of sets $V\mapsto\{$locally constant maps $V\cap C\to R\}$ on $T$ (restriction of maps as restriction maps). Put $\mathcal A=(i_W)_*\underline R_W$ on $Y$ and $\mathcal B=(i_Z)_*\underline R_Z$ on $X$, and let $f_*\mathcal B$ be the direct image, $f_*\mathcal B(V)=\mathcal B(f^{-1}V)$. The maps $\alpha_V:\mathcal A(V)\to\mathcal B(f^{-1}V)$, $g\mapsto g\circ f|_{f^{-1}(V)\cap Z}$ ($V\subseteq Y$ open; well defined since $f(f^{-1}(V)\cap Z)\subseteq V\cap W$ and a locally constant map composed with a continuous map is locally constant) form a morphism of sheaves $\alpha:\mathcal A\to f_*\mathcal B$. Let $f^{-1}$ be the inverse image of sheaves of sets with the unit $\eta_{\mathcal A}:\mathcal A\to f_*f^{-1}\mathcal A$ of the adjunction $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$, as in [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (2), (3) with values in sets (the adjunction for sheaves of sets is [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-colimits-finite-products] (a)), and let $\alpha^\flat:f^{-1}\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be the morphism corresponding to $\alpha$, i.e. the unique morphism of sheaves of sets with $\alpha^\flat_{f^{-1}V}\circ\eta_{\mathcal A,V}=\alpha_V$ for every open $V\subseteq Y$. Then $\alpha^\flat$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of sets on $X$; in particular it is bijective on sections over every open subset of $X$.

proof.text: *Step 1 (the objects).* By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-constant-stalks] (0), applied to $(Y,W,R)$ and to $(X,Z,R)$, $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ are sheaves of sets, hence so is $f_*\mathcal B$ [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (1) (with values in sets). Each $\alpha_V$ is well defined by the reasons given in the statement, and for opens $V'\subseteq V$ of $Y$ and $g\in\mathcal A(V)$ we have $(g\circ f|_{f^{-1}(V)\cap Z})|_{f^{-1}(V')\cap Z}=g|_{V'\cap W}\circ f|_{f^{-1}(V')\cap Z}$, so $\alpha$ is a morphism of sheaves $\mathcal A\to f_*\mathcal B$. By the adjunction $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ for sheaves of sets [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-colimits-finite-products] (a), whose unit is $\eta_{\mathcal A,V}=\theta_{f^{-1}V}\circ\iota^{f^{-1}V}_V$ [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (3), there is exactly one morphism $\alpha^\flat:f^{-1}\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ with $\alpha^\flat_{f^{-1}V}\circ\eta_{\mathcal A,V}=\alpha_V$ for all open $V\subseteq Y$.

source.place: Sheaves, Definition Tag 006W and Lemma Tag 00AE (line 4936); adjunction of Section Tag 008C (presheaves-functorial); the compatibility computation is written by the agent

proof.text: *Step 2 (the stalk map of $\alpha^\flat$ on germs).* Fix $x\in X$ and put $y=f(x)$. Stalks, germs and induced stalk maps $\varphi_x(s_x)=(\varphi_U(s))_x$ are as in [lem-weil-pbc-sets-sheaf-iso-on-stalks]. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-stalk] (applied to the sheaf of sets $\mathcal A$ on $Y$) there is a bijection $c:\mathcal A_y\to(f^{-1}\mathcal A)_x$ with $c(g_y)=(\eta_{\mathcal A,V}(g))_x$ for every open $V\ni y$ and $g\in\mathcal A(V)$. For such $V,g$ (note $x\in f^{-1}V$), using the definition of the stalk map and $\alpha^\flat_{f^{-1}V}\circ\eta_{\mathcal A,V}=\alpha_V$ (Step 1): $\alpha^\flat_x(c(g_y))=\alpha^\flat_x((\eta_{\mathcal A,V}(g))_x)=(\alpha^\flat_{f^{-1}V}(\eta_{\mathcal A,V}(g)))_x=(\alpha_V(g))_x=(g\circ f|_{f^{-1}(V)\cap Z})_x$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 008H (lemma-stalk-pullback, line 2197) and Section Tag 0078 (stalks, line 894: the map on stalks induced by a morphism)

proof.text: *Step 3 (points of $Z$).* Let $x\in Z$, so $y=f(x)\in W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-constant-stalks] (a), applied to $(Y,W,R)$ at $y$ and to $(X,Z,R)$ at $x$, the maps $\mathrm{ev}_y:\mathcal A_y\to R$, $g_y\mapsto g(y)$, and $\mathrm{ev}_x:\mathcal B_x\to R$, $h_x\mapsto h(x)$, are bijective. By Step 2, for every open $V\ni y$ and $g\in\mathcal A(V)$: $\mathrm{ev}_x(\alpha^\flat_x(c(g_y)))=(g\circ f)(x)=g(y)=\mathrm{ev}_y(g_y)$. Two maps out of the colimit $\mathcal A_y$ that agree after every coprojection are equal [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], so $\mathrm{ev}_x\circ\alpha^\flat_x\circ c=\mathrm{ev}_y$, i.e. $\alpha^\flat_x=\mathrm{ev}_x^{-1}\circ\mathrm{ev}_y\circ c^{-1}$ is a composite of bijections, hence bijective.

source.place: Sheaves, Example Tag 007B (line 995) and Lemma Tag 00AE (line 4936), case x in Z; written out by the agent

proof.text: *Step 4 (points outside $Z$).* Let $x\in X\setminus Z$, so $y=f(x)\notin W$ (as $Z=f^{-1}(W)$). By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-constant-stalks] (b), applied to $(Y,W,R)$ at $y$, $\mathcal A_y$ has exactly one element, hence so has $(f^{-1}\mathcal A)_x$, which is in bijection with it by $c$ (Step 2); by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-constant-stalks] (b), applied to $(X,Z,R)$ at $x$, $\mathcal B_x$ has exactly one element. A map between two one-element sets is bijective, so $\alpha^\flat_x$ is bijective.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 00AE (line 4936), case x not in Z

proof.text: *Step 5 (conclusion).* By Steps 3 and 4, $\alpha^\flat_x:(f^{-1}\mathcal A)_x\to\mathcal B_x$ is bijective for every $x\in X$; since $f^{-1}\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ are sheaves of sets on $X$, [lem-weil-pbc-sets-sheaf-iso-on-stalks] shows that $\alpha^\flat$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of sets, i.e. has an inverse morphism $\psi$ with $\psi\circ\alpha^\flat=\mathrm{id}$ and $\alpha^\flat\circ\psi=\mathrm{id}$; evaluating these identities on an open $U\subseteq X$ shows that $\alpha^\flat_U$ is bijective with inverse $\psi_U$.

lean.statement: theorem inverse_image_closed_pushforward_constant (X Y : TopCat.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Y) (W : Set Y) (hW : IsClosed W) (R : Type u) : let Z : Set X := f ⁻¹' W let P : Y.Presheaf (Type u) := { obj := fun V ↦ LocallyConstant {y : Y // y ∈ unop V ∧ y ∈ W} R map := fun {U V} i ↦ TypeCat.ofHom (LocallyConstant.comap ⟨fun y : {y : Y // y ∈ unop V ∧ y ∈ W} ↦ ⟨y.1, i.unop.le y.2.1, y.2.2⟩, continuous_subtype_val.subtype_mk _⟩) map_id := by intros; rfl map_comp := by intros; rfl } let Q : X.Presheaf (Type u) := { obj := fun U ↦ LocallyConstant {x : X // x ∈ unop U ∧ x ∈ Z} R map := fun {U V} i ↦ TypeCat.ofHom (LocallyConstant.comap ⟨fun x : {x : X // x ∈ unop V ∧ x ∈ Z} ↦ ⟨x.1, i.unop.le x.2.1, x.2.2⟩, continuous_subtype_val.subtype_mk _⟩) map_id := by intros; rfl map_comp := by intros; rfl } ∃ (hP : P.IsSheaf) (hQ : Q.IsSheaf), let A : Y.Sheaf (Type u) := ⟨P, hP⟩ let B : X.Sheaf (Type u) := ⟨Q, hQ⟩ let L := Sheaf.pullback (Type u) f let adj : L ⊣ Sheaf.pushforward (Type u) f := Sheaf.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (Type u) f ∃ alpha : A ⟶ (Sheaf.pushforward (Type u) f).obj B, (∀ (V : Opens Y) (g : P.obj (op V)), alpha.hom.app (op V) g = LocallyConstant.comap ⟨fun x : {x : X // x ∈ (Opens.map f).obj V ∧ x ∈ Z} ↦ ⟨f x.1, x.2.1, x.2.2⟩, (f.hom.continuous.comp continuous_subtype_val).subtype_mk _⟩ g) ∧ let beta := (adj.homEquiv A B).symm alpha IsIso beta ∧ (∀ U : Opens X, Function.Bijective (beta.hom.app (op U))) ∧ (∀ (V : Opens Y) (g : P.obj (op V)), beta.hom.app (op ((Opens.map f).obj V)) ((adj.unit.app A).hom.app (op V) g) = alpha.hom.app (op V) g) ∧ (∀ beta' : L.obj A ⟶ B, (∀ (V : Opens Y) (g : P.obj (op V)), beta'.hom.app (op ((Opens.map f).obj V)) ((adj.unit.app A).hom.app (op V) g) = alpha.hom.app (op V) g) → beta' = beta)
